title: Server Security and Authentication
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of server security and authentication in a Swift program or workflow.
Apply authentication and authorization in a small, inspectable example.
Check the expected result and identify one boundary case or platform constraint.

content.intro: This lesson focuses on server security and authentication and the practical choices around it. Start with the smallest example, connect it to “Authentication and authorization”, and verify the result before adding complexity.
content.why_it_matters: Specialist paths and new language features depend on target support and toolchain details. Treat official documentation and reproducible checks as part of the solution.

content_blocks.title: Application Security Boundaries
content_blocks.alt_text: The diagram shows untrusted input passing through validation and authorization, while diagnostics avoid exposing secrets.
content_blocks.caption: Treat external values and secrets deliberately.

content_blocks.text: **Start with the rule.** Treat input from files, networks, and users as untrusted. Validate at boundaries, enforce authorization server-side, protect credentials, minimize retained data, and redact logs.

**Work through the lesson.** Choose a specialist track and validate its target-specific toolchain, APIs, runtime, and deployment model. The detailed subtopic list in this lesson preserves the curriculum coverage; treat each item as a cue for a small example or a focused question rather than trying to memorize syntax.

items.title: Authentication and authorization
items.text: Treat input from files, networks, and users as untrusted. Validate at boundaries, enforce authorization server-side, protect credentials, minimize retained data, and redact logs.

items.title: Request validation
items.text: Network operations can fail or return non-success HTTP statuses even when transport succeeds. Validate responses, decode data safely, set timeouts, and model loading/error/cancellation states.

items.title: Rate limiting concepts
items.text: Treat rate limiting concepts as a specialist or version-sensitive area. Verify target support and toolchain assumptions first, isolate platform-specific code, and document limitations instead of treating experimental support as universal.

content_blocks.title: Keep in mind
content_blocks.text: Use the compiler and versioned documentation as evidence. Do not treat a source-string check or an illustrative output as proof that a complete Swift program compiles on every platform.
